name.text: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 June 2024 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending Regulations (EC) No 300/2008, (EU) No 167/2013, (EU) No 168/2013, (EU) 2018/858, (EU) 2018/1139 and (EU) 2019/2144 and Directives 2014/90/EU, (EU) 2016/797 and (EU) 2020/1828 (Artificial Intelligence Act)

summary.text: Before first using a high-risk AI system to evaluate creditworthiness or credit scores of natural persons, or for risk assessment and pricing in life and health insurance, the firm must assess the impact on fundamental rights: the processes and period of use, the people affected, the specific risks of harm, human oversight and the measures if risks materialise. It notifies the market surveillance authority of the results on the template, updates the assessment when elements change, and may cross-refer to its GDPR data protection impact assessment. Systems placed on the market or put into service before 2 December 2027 are caught only if their design changes significantly afterwards.

It notifies the market surveillance authority of the results on the template, updates the assessment when elements change, and may cross-refer to its GDPR data protection impact assessment. Systems placed on the market or put into service before 2 December 2027 are caught only if their design changes significantly afterwards.

title.text: Use high-risk AI systems according to their instructions, with human oversight and monitoring

name.text: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 June 2024 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending Regulations (EC) No 300/2008, (EU) No 167/2013, (EU) No 168/2013, (EU) 2018/858, (EU) 2018/1139 and (EU) 2019/2144 and Directives 2014/90/EU, (EU) 2016/797 and (EU) 2020/1828 (Artificial Intelligence Act)

summary.text: As a deployer of a high-risk AI system the firm must use it in line with the provider's instructions, assign human oversight to competent, trained persons with authority, ensure input data it controls are relevant and representative, monitor operation, suspend use and inform the provider and authority of risks and serious incidents, keep the logs it controls for at least six months, and inform workers' representatives and affected workers before workplace use. A financial institution meets the monitoring duty through its internal governance rules and keeps the logs within its financial-services documentation. Systems placed on the market or put into service before 2 December 2027 are caught only if their design changes significantly afterwards.

A financial institution meets the monitoring duty through its internal governance rules and keeps the logs within its financial-services documentation. Systems placed on the market or put into service before 2 December 2027 are caught only if their design changes significantly afterwards.
